doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Count Basie's bandstand signals
summary: Basie used eyebrow raises, head tilts and shoulder lifts to direct Butch, and never signalled displeasure.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Did Basie ever like raise his eyebrows and give you a look that you interpreted as, I’m not going to do that again.

No he didn’t, and that’s a good question too. Basie had a series of signals that he would give to me. Raising the eyebrows was one. Raising the eyebrows meant to increase the volume or to get ready for the explosion. That’s how — that’s how physical he would become on the bandstand. You know, we’re not talking Stan Kenton and waving the arms from wall to wall. Basie had a minimum of motion to give me direction. Sometimes when we were playing he would tilt his head. That’s where he’d want the beat, on two and four. He’d want me to accent that and make it stronger. Sometimes he would raise his shoulders when we would come in on an explosion like at the beginning of “All of Me.” And that was the signal to let it rip. There were a few things like that.

But he never, ever gave me any sort of information or looks or direction that said he was unhappy with what I was doing or don’t do that. That leads to a story, I have got to tell you this story, you’ve drawn me into it.
